key_insight: Ceramics derive their performance from tightly coupled bonding, processing, microstructure, and defects, making property control possible but brittle failure difficult to avoid.
engineering_relevance: Understanding and tuning densification, porosity, grain size, and phase stability is essential for designing durable structural, functional, and biomedical ceramic components.
method: Review of the processing–microstructure–property–performance relationship in ceramics
Comparison of conventional sintering, sol–gel processing, and additive manufacturing
Coverage of biomedical, smart, nanoceramic, and composite ceramic systems
evidence_signal: The paper synthesizes reported relationships between composition, defects, microstructure, and properties across ceramic classes rather than presenting a new experimental dataset.
watch_item: A major implementation challenge is the porosity–strength trade-off, along with brittle fracture and processing heterogeneity that can undermine scalability.
paper_title: Ceramic Materials: From Atomic Bonding and Processing to Microstructure, Functional Properties, and Biomedical Applications
